tips.comment: The 2yo was a good runner-up on his debut three weeks ago, posting a decent RPR rating. The 3rd in that race has boosted the form since, and the winner holds a Group 2 entry. He should be a player in this novice stakes contest, and he receives a big 7lb pull in the weights from the favorite.

Won 7 runner race on debut over CD back in May & then connections decided the Coventry would be the next hurdle but unfortunately the tip finished last but given an easy time . Travels back up to familiar ground & despite giving the rivals 7Lb should be well in the mix once again now dropping back in class .

Cosmic Clarets is a 2yo colt trained by Richard Fahey. He is out of a Listed-placed sprinter, Imtiyaaz (IRE), and displayed considerable promise when second on debut. Imtiyaaz (IRE) was related to seven individual winners, two of which, Bunker 107, won a listed race, and Imperial Fighter 112 (placed in three group races). The owner of the dam, Imtiyaaz, trained by Roger Varian, M Al-Qatami & K M Al-Mudhaf, have had 18 juvenile winners in the UK and landed 11 big race wins in the UK and abroad with horses of all ages. This suggests they have a good eye for talented fillies and mares, and Cosmic Clarets has the potential to be above average. Jockey Oisin Orr is 51/307 wins for Richard Fahey with a 17% win strike rate, so Cosmic Clarets is in good hands and looks a tad overpriced at 9-2.
Kevin Ryan has high hopes for Nursia who holds a Gimcrack entry, which suggests he has shown some talent at home. It could be worth taking a chance on him to make a winning start here.
This one will be fitter for the debut run, and they have got a good jockey booking/change. Worth a small each-way saver bet.
The 3-year-old won by 9 lengths at Ripon last week and is validated by the time figure, implying that a 6lb penalty could very well be inadequate to prevent her next victory.

The 4yo has been below par this year but shaped better three weeks ago when finishing 4th, a little keen early in the race but he saw the 6f trip out nicely and the form looks solid. A 3lb lower mark and a strong jockey change for today. He ran plenty of nice races last year including going close over this 6f C/D last Oct while racing off a huge 16lb higher mark.

Has scored 2 wins over C&D and started to move in the right direction again, especially after a credible effort LTO when 4th of 10 at Carlisle earlier this month. Just 1lb higher than last winning mark, so I do fancy his chances tomorrow.

On a very quiet day's racing, I will take a look at SIXCOR at the price. It just looks to be running well and shouldn't be fazed by the step up in trip. Strong chance of placing, but let's go hard or go home...

Rory has been in terrible form this season. He normally misses the break, then finishes strongly, but he hasn't really finished off any of his recent starts. Maybe he's just not in love with the game any longer, but Jim Goldie has a way of getting this type of horse back in contention, and I wouldn't give up on him just yet. His mark is as low as it's ever been, so if he manages a bit of a revival, he could place at a fair price.

Been sent off favorite in her last 2 races and failed to deliver, but returns to good ground and returns to Ayr where she seems to run her best races. Handicap mark unchanged on 71, and although her last winning mark was 69, it still looks competitive in a weak race.

Our Absent Friends looks to have a strong each way chance here. This 7-year-old has run some solid races off this similar mark. Returns here under favorable conditions, and can ignore the last time out run as amateur jockeys are never one to judge a horse on. What boosts my confidence is the trainer/jockey strike rate together, 36% at Ayr, which is very eye-catching to say the least. Looks a solid each way option with a big chance of winning.

Just five career runs for the 3yo and still unexposed. Runner-up twice and a novice stakes win at the start of this month. He posted a high RPR rating for that win and if the Racing Post are correct with their assessment then he has a big chance off this 75 handicap mark today.

Cargin Bhui is a 4-year-old gelding trained by David & Nicola Barron. He is 1/11 wins and hasn't won since his win over 5f on the AW on his second start. He opened on a mark of 82 and runs today off a career-low handicap mark of 71, having proved rather disappointing over 6-7f. He hasn't been sent off bigger than 10-1 in his last six starts and posted a career-high RPR of 86 just six starts back when beaten 3/4l by Ziggy's Condor over 6f. He often races prominently and shows plenty of pace and is dropped down to 5f for the first time in eight starts. Joe Fanning rides, and he often likes to race prominently and often leads. His charge, Cargin Bhui, could lead his rivals a merry dance and lead from pillar to post.

A challenging 7 year old, yet a 4 time course victor who increased his win rate at Hamilton in June. Recently finished 4th in a handicap at Hamilton 18 days ago, starting very slowly. The Jim Goldie stable is performing well, and with a skilled jockey like Lauren Young, boasting a 16% strike rate and a valuable 7lb claim, the gelding presents a solid each-way bet at 12/1.
Not beaten far in this class on last 2 runs and won a class 6 handicap over C/D on prior run. Only 1lb higher here and very good jockey/trainer combination, makes current 10/1 solid Ew value here.
A beaten favourite over a mile and a quarter under today's jockey last week and should welcome this drop in trip being a former course and distance winner in May 2025.

In search of a hat-trick after her successes at Musselburgh in the last few weeks, winning over 7f and 1m. She represents a notable risk, and a 4lb increase is unlikely to stop her from making a strong challenge.

Taking a chance with Zebra Star. Has been consistent as of late. Did no favors LTO running too freely. Down to a workable mark and at the price looks a good each way play. Stiff mile should suit and weather forecast for some rain early doors, so should make the ground conditions perfect.

Not been beaten far in their last 4 flat runs, between 8.5f/10f and is still nicely treated here off current mark of 59. Fast run race in this mile event would suit, good jockey retains ride and shrewd trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 16 percent, making current 7.50 solid Ew value in the race.
Trainer Dianne Sayer's horses are running at a 'running to form' rate of 82% and this leads us to DETECTIVE. Top rated by 2 clear points and with a recent win under his belt, this looks a solid bet.

Homer Stokes ran a fair race at Carlisle last time, beaten by a more lightly raced horse who finished second here last week. The third in the Carlisle race came out and won next time, giving the overall look of that form a fairly solid look for the grade. There appears to be rain in the forecast, and that would definitely add to the chances as he is best with some ease in the ground.

Trais Fluors has been in my notes since October 2023, and although the veteran has won only four of his twenty-four races since, I think he has an e.w. chance as long as there's eight in this race. Interesting to see trainer Linda Perratt has two runners.
Winner at Ripon in May. Good efforts in a pair of class 4s at York and Beverley since but should appreciate this drop back into class 5 and therefore run very well this afternoon.
This 10-year-old has had a fantastic season with a hat trick of wins here at Ayr in April and May. Although a no-show at Hamilton last time, he wasn't given a hard time when his chances were gone.

The Jim Goldie trained 6 year old C&D winner SOPHIESTICATE looks worth an each way interest having dropped to 8lb below her last winning mark. She will be fit on her fourth start back from an extended 564-day break and has a decent apprentice taking a useful 7lb off her back.

Small each-way chance for Cisco Disco who needs improvement but that is possible. Signs of a return to some better form when finishing 2nd last time out, this horse usually follows up 1 good performance with another so from what is still a fair and competitive looking rating, he looks capable of running well today.

Has been performing in Germany until switching to flat in the U.K. and started extremely well, winning debut run in the U.K. for new yard at Musselburgh last October. But did not have the best run LTO at the same course in handicap debut over here last November. With a dropped mark, I think she can bounce back strongly if she can overcome rustiness due to an 8-month absence.

Ajdayet ended last term with a C5 win and returned from a break last month running for a new yard after having wind surgery in a C4. He was a bit duff but may have needed the run. He has dropped to his last AW winning mark and is worth another try now second up, which is when I would expect to see more after wind surgery and back in C5 EW.
Still a maiden after nineteen runs, Elemental Eye was just nipped when a clear of the rest second BF last time out. Although up a pound for that run, a repeat should see him thereabouts.

This is probably the poorest race Beltane has run in for a while, and it provides him with a great opportunity to claim a win. He was a fair third at Beverley last time. However, his third at Carlisle before that was the form that stands out in the context of this race. He was behind two very in-form horses that day, and a repeat of that running will see him home here.

Gelded son of Justify & Rumplestiltskin ( Dam's sire Danehill ) who was last seen at Newcastle 17 days ago where finishing 10th/14 in a race that wasn't the best of run to suit however this race is a whole different scenario one of which J S Goldie's inmate can really benefit as a good analysis of this class 6 handicap clearly shows Spun To Gold will be well suited in a race of this nature and should also have his favoured pace level at his disposal given the horses enrolled to run here which will play really well into his strengths especially here at the Ayr track currently operating on a rapidly easing mark of 57 Spun To Gold looks poised for a big run here and is capable of taking advantage of his rapidly easing mark jockey P Mulrennan takes the ride and can give Spun To Gold the perfect ride here at Ayr must be considered of this sort of mark

Centara has been a force under Jay Tidball, cruising to two wide-margin wins. This is over a track which has already been won on, and it's just about handling the rise in weight, which I think Centara will do.

The model I run suggests Magistrato can win this one. Magistrato lines up here with the second highest RPR of this smaller 5 horse field but has the lowest official ranking of them all. This leaves Magistrato carrying the lowest initial amount of weight around this 2m round trip. Last out 31 days ago and came second off the back of some really solid placing form. Figures of 3224-2 and needs to show a bit more to get over the line in this small field. Fitness shouldn't be a concern having only raced 31 days ago. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Queen Kate ran a superb race to finish a close-up fourth in the Aintree Champion Mares Bumper, with the first four well clear of a high-class looking field. She has a penalty to carry, but unless there is an exceptional newcomer, she will win this.

What A Peach ran a decent race in what turned into quite a competitive little bumper at Stratford last time. Wasn't beaten far there, showing significant improvement on first outing. Should run a decent race. Tom Broughton claims 5lbs for Barry Brennan. Fancied to run well at odds of 12-1.

The model I run suggests Get The Value can win this one. Get The Value lines up here with the second highest RPR of the small 4 horse field. Has the lowest official ranking by quite an amount, and that leaves Get The Value carrying far less weight than the other 3 runners. Has got some form to back it up and has figures of PP1-12 and has managed to put a string together of good runs. Prior course winner and a prior distance winner but hasn't put the two together yet. Maybe tomorrow getting over the line first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Ollie Pears prepares Maax Of Stars, and with top rider Sam Twiston-Davies taking the reins on the likely favourite, they look set to get the thick end of the purse this time of asking after some good recent efforts from this handy mare. Course and distance winner previously.
Won round here over shorter on penultimate start before just getting collared on follow-up bid from 6lb extra. Goes up another 4lb here and is upped in trip. Form horse and has a chance if staying.

The model I run suggests Sassified can win this one. Sassified lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 7-horse field but has an official ranking which is second last, and leaves Sassified looking very well treated off this mark. Steps out carrying the second lowest amount of initial weight and has the form to go with it. Prior figures of 228-31 and with the last win coming only 31 days ago, race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Thahab Ifraj is a 12-year-old chestnut gelding trained by Alexandra Dunn with Mr. Jack Andrews claiming 3lb, holding a win rate of 13% and place rate of 20% from 51 starts on similar ground here. He returned to form last time out when beaten by just a length over 2m1f at this track off a mark of 96, showing his usual front-running style and only collared late on. He is now back below his last winning mark and has a decent record in this grade, with six prior wins in handicaps. His course form is a bit patchy, but he handled it well last time and gets the same conditions to ride on again today. If allowed to dictate, I reckon he could prove hard to get past and in my book he is a definite each-way claim with a chance of the win here

Songo is a 9-year-old gelding trained by Richard Hawker and ridden by Robert Dunne. £14.73 profit with Hawker. He is a two-time winner over hurdles (course winner), both wins coming on today's good ground over further, but has won on the flat (7/18 wins). Songo is a useful dual-purpose horse over 1m 6f, so today's trip and ground suit him. In his last win, he posted a career-high RPR of 119, beating Donnie Azoff (108) by 11 lengths in a class 3 contest. Donnie Azoff has won three times since and is rated 119. Songo is also clearly well handicapped off 103 in a lowly Class 5 under Robert Dunne for the very first time. Songo also comes to hand this time of year, winning five times in July/August.

the model I run suggests Mister Upton can win this one. Mister Upton lines up with a comparably high RPR to the other 3 runners in this small field, but has by far the lowest official ranking. Subsequently steps out carrying 12 lbs less to the nearest in weights and over 1 stone less to the top weight. Tries the blinkers for the first time to aid concentration and looks for improvement with the headgear. Early market suggests very close race. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Tom Broughton's five-pound claim could make all the difference here, given that his main rival, Time To Bite, has previously looked vulnerable with big weights. That was a solid second last time out and set to go one better here.
Debut over hurdles. Should take this. Went off as favorite when taking a flat race over the course. If taking to hurdles, should be good enough.
Decent flat handicapper who dons some new headgear for this hurdles debut. There have been a few strong whispers emanating from in and around the stable, so this is my NB selection.

ROADSHOW has been placed in a hurdle race from five NH starts. Also won a flat race, unseated rider in a hurdle race over 2m 1f at Newton Abbot on his latest outing last month. Upped in trip to 2m 2f should suit and could well be able to win this race.

The model I run suggests Old Bridge can cause an upset and win this one. Old Bridge lines up here as the youngest horse but has the highest RPR of the 7-runner field. Steps out carrying the joint lowest amount of weight around this 2m 2f maiden hurdle. Runs well on quicker ground and a decent second at Bangor on Dee when running on Good to Firm, which is what is forecast for Newton Abbot. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by a small gap back to second in the race simulation but the good value on offer here at 15s.
India Love is a fast ground 5f specialist. She has won recently at York and Lingfield and is capable of completing the hat-trick here for George Bhouey.

Museum Piece is a 2-year-old filly trained by Michael Bell. She went 2-1 on AW, winning her maiden by beating Flowerhead by an easy 3.5 lengths. Flowerhead has since finished runner-up in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot and is now rated 100. She then ran in a novice stakes and finished 4/11 again at Kempton after a poor turf debut, bumped at the start but still grabbed the lead giving the winner Sayidah Hard Spun 5 lbs (who won again last week RPR 85) and gave 7 lbs to the 2/11 Mystic Moment, who has since finished 2-2-1 and posted an RPR of 85. The 7/11 No Spritz No Party, 8.25 lengths behind the winner, won next time out in a maiden at Pontefract at 33-1, so solid form. She returned for the turf for a second time in her last start and produced a personal best RPR of 79. Museum Piece, who has plenty of early a pace, could skip away in this small field.off a workable mark of 75 under Hector Crouch. Hector rides well for Bell, being 43/206 wins, showing an LSP of £15.35, and looks a tad a overpriced at 8-1.

This A M Balding trained 3-year-old gelding won for the first time in his latest start over one mile two furlongs on good to firm ground at Doncaster. When running on strongly inside the final furlong, he beat the C Johnston trained Elsass by a neck. With Oisin Murphy doing the steering, he can follow up today.

Amazonian Dream is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Rod Millman, who has won with 4 of his last 12 runners. Oisin Murphy rides this 3-time CD winner, and Oisin has won on his last two CD wins and at Sandown. His last win came at Kempton off 89, so he looks well handicapped. He has not performed in the same vein this season but drops in class and is reunited with Oisin, a jockey who does well with Millman. On balance, they have won 51 races together and show a healthy LSP of £28.28 from 301 rides. Today could be a good time to catch Amazonian Dream with conditions to suit off a 7lb lower mark at Kempton and 2lb below his last CD win.

A beaten favorite over 7 furlongs at Epsom 12 days ago, leading until headed 2 out and no extra close to home, 3rd of 8. Drops in trip and reunited with Hollie Doyle, who rode him to victory over 7 furlongs 3 races ago at Lingfield.

Mehmar has not won since last July and August, with the latter being off an 87 and changed yards in May. He has had two down-the-pack runs in C3 but drops to C4 today off an 82 and could be worth a shot EW.

This Ollie Sangster-trained filly did well to only be beaten one length in second behind the R Hannon-trained Lebron Power over this course and distance 21 days ago, despite being slowly away at the start and then finding trouble in running. So with Oisin Murphy back onboard, she looks hard to beat.

Warning Symbol is a 2-year-old colt trained by James Owen and makes his debut. He is a second foal related to Wimbledon Hawkeye (trained by James Owen), who won on his 2-year-old debut and later won the Group 2 Royal Lodge at Newmarket and ran well in the 2000 Guineas again at headquarters, rated 112. He is out of a dam, Eva Maria (Richard Fahey), who was quite forward, winning 3 of her 5 opening races. Owners of the dam, Eva Maria, W J and T C O Gredley, have had 72 juvenile winners in the UK with various trainers and 16 big race winners over both codes and all ages, including two-time Group winner, the 117-rated James Garfield. James Owen is an upwardly mobile trainer who is being given plenty of opportunities from successful owners and has had 179 winners if sent off in the top two in the betting since 2023. The owner of the dam Eva Maria, W J and T C O Gredley, clearly have some good talent in finding useful fillies and mares, and Warning Symbol has the potential to be as smart as his sibling Wimbledon Hawkeye, sired by 2000 Guineas winner Kameko.

Lohoobb made a big improvement last time out when second up and dropping to C5 to grab second on the run-in. I would expect a bit more today with David Probert to help out, who is on a bit of a roll at the moment.

Shams is a well-bred Blue Point filly who was dropped into a hot race on debut. She didn't run the best, but I think the ability is there and she should progress with each run. She's drawn well, and the ground/track will suit. If she improves from last time out, I'd be hopeful of hitting the frame and getting a place.
Competizione was second in 2 of his past 3 races both of them in the class 4 and he can win today this class 5 Novice Stakes here at Windsor.

Strobelight is a strong value play at Windsor, having shaped better than the bare result last time in a race that hasn't stopped producing winners. He travelled smoothly for a long way before fading late, suggesting the drop back in trip and a more prominent ride could see him in a much better light.

Has not been able to beat a rival in the 2 runs to date, finishing last in both runs. But the debut run was on AW, and then the switch to turf LTO made life harder. So, hoping now with some stable factors (turf, similar conditions & same class) makes the difference.

An each-way play here in this 9-runner field with Chalta against a 2-9f Competizione, which will probably hose up. Chalta made her debut on AW at 150-1 and finished last of seven. She is a 4yo filly trained by Sheena West and ridden by Trevor Whelan. They make a good team with 14/92 wins and 23/92 places and are 4/14 wins at Windsor when combining. Chalta is upped to a mile today and makes her turf debut. She is a half-sister to Pomme Pomme, who won five consecutive races YTD, rising from a mark of 47 to 80 in the handicap. They are both out of a dam called Apple Anni (IRE), who won on her second start at Beverley over 7.5f. So, Sheena West has something to work with, but in all probability, she is looking for a handicap mark through qualifying. However, this is a weak maiden. Trevor Whelan has been riding well of late, picking up a winner yesterday, and this is his only ride of the day. He waits until 19:30 to ride a 100-1 for a trainer he has a close affiliation with in recent years - intriguing!

Sheikh Raj is a 3-year-old gelding making a stable debut for Richard Hughes. He clearly has had training problems, having had wind surgery and a 225-day break. He runs off 74 today, which could prove to be a workable mark based on his debut run, beaten by Yaroogh (RPR 89). Sheikh Raj finished 2/13. Yaroogh has since won a class 2 handicap, a Listed race in France, and finished 2/8 in a Group 3 and is now rated 104. A set of new stable surroundings could unearth any underlying issues and could go close to breaking his maiden tag at the fifth time of asking under Billy Loughnane, who is 3/11 wins for Hughes and still basking in their July Cup Group 1 win with No Half Measures at 66-1.

Art Patron can get off the mark here. Best run was LTO after being upped in trip and at this course and distance. Looks like the right race to break its maiden with Oisin Murphy riding. Should be the one to beat.

Bravo Zulu tends to do most of his winning on the AW but returned from a short break last month to two runs on turf with its lower mark. He won when second up, and while taking on 4 lbs for that, he is still 8 lbs below his last AW winning mark. So, I would expect him to be involved again today.

There's not a lot of class 4 form on show here. Newfangled hasn't attempted this level since being a 2 year old but has proven course and distance form. Yard are in good form and go well at Windsor too.

Adorla of Achill is a lightly exposed 3-year-old filly stepping back into a handicap where she has already shown her ability. She won a Haydock Class 5 handicap back in May. Dropping slightly in the weights and racing on an ideal trip, she looks well treated and poised to be sharper for this outing. The stable is in decent enough form, and this could be a nice spot to capitalize before the market catches on.

At the top third of the handicap mark in this field and did not have the best of runs here LTO over C&D when 4 of 5 last month. But he's a 2-time C&D winner and the last 2 runs have been here and now 4 lbs higher than the last winning mark. Represents good value considering he's a threat.

Benvenuto Cellini is a 2-year-old colt trained by A P O'Brien. He has strong form claims on his second at the Curragh and looks sure to improve on that. Being a second foal and a full brother to Giselle, a Listed winner also trained by A P O'Brien out of a dam Newspaperofrecord (IRE), owned by Klaravich Stables Inc (produced 50+ big race winners), he won four Group contests including two Group 1's, which included the Breeders' Cup Juvenile at Churchill Downs in 2018 by an impressive 6.75 lengths an like Frankel remained unbeaten as a juvenile. Benvenuto Cellini's connections must be excited about his future, which is probably going to be extremely bright given his impeccable pedigree line. Not the most original of selections at such diminutive odds and could end up being as short as 1-4 when the big hitters start wager but is my short-priced banker of the day.
Trainer shows a whopping 59% win rate at this course with 2-year-olds. Jockey shows a whopping 54% win rate at this course with 2-year-olds.

Former point and bumper winner Full Confession finished 2nd here last month in his first hurdle, where he would have been closer but for some novicey jumping. Patrick Mullins takes over the ride, and he should win.

Mr. P W Mullins has a 34.5% win strike rate for W P Mullins and rides Full Confession, a 1/2f off 11st 12lb. Jack Kennedy has a 16.8% win strike rate for Gordon Elliott and rides Power Of Word. Full Confession finished runner-up last time out posting a career-high RPR of 123. The winner won at Perth yesterday by 6.5l. Power Of Words finished runner-up at Perth last start and posted a career- high RPR of 104. 'Took keen hold, led, raced wide on turn after 5th, hampered by loose horse just before 6th, soon headed, led again 2 out, headed and no extra run-in' over 2m 4f. So, Full Confession has around a 7lb advantage, having to give his younger counterpart 12lb (weight for age allowance). Todays drop in trip in a first-time hood (took hold at Perth using up valuable energy, raced wide, and got hampered by a loose horse, so did well in the circumstances) and Jack Kennedy replacesnKevin Sexton, will bring about some significant improvement - Kennedy and Elliott are 3/6 wins on horses.i a first time hood/visor and 3/3 if sent off as favourite which is unlikely.

A Castle Du Berlais gelding who is closely related to the fairly useful hurdler and smart chaser, Fracky Du Berlais. He placed in his last of 3 point starts but had a disappointing performance, coming in 14th in a novice hurdle at Bellewstown during his NH debut 9 days ago. He has a lot to improve upon, but that recent run will have been beneficial, and the jockey's 7lb claim will certainly be an asset. A small each-way bet at 66/1 looks like a promising option.

Ar Nos Na Gaoithe is a 6-year-old mare trained by P J Rothwell and ridden by Tiernan Power Roche (ridden 25 winners for P J Rothwell) with a 5lb claim. She runs off 85 and comes here in good form, having finished 2/12 over CD last time out, finishing 2/11 behind Prolagnan, beaten 1/2 length (led going easily last, ridden but headed run-in, kept on towards finish (op 17/2 touched 9/2), posting a career-high RPR of 90 off 88 and 81 (7lb conditional on board), better than her 6.5 length win at Clonmel in a handicap hurdle. So essentially, she is 4lb higher today. The form has been bolstered with the winner Pralognan winning a 1m 4.5f Newcastle flat handicap on the next start, and despite a 4lb rise, she should see it in her stride and add further funds to her connections' account balance.
Down 3 pounds and back on his favored good ground here. Given he is fit enough to do himself justice after a break, he has a decent chance to be in the frame.

Considering she was returning from a 175 day break I thought James Fahey's 6 year old Mare DEMANDING JERRY ran a decent race & was throwing down the gauntlet & was still there round about 17½ furlongs before understandably fading. This Daughter of MASTEROFTHEHORSE drops 2lbs & gets in form Jockey Kevin Sexton (47.37% place strike rate the past month) who also has a decent record here in Northern Ireland with a 42.86% place strike rate the past year. Trainer isn't doing too badly either with a 66.67% place strike rate the past month with his runners. Should this Mare have Shaken off the hoof rust at 16/1 with 4 places I'm more than happy to have a small piece of the pie.

The model I run suggests Centaq can win this one. Centaq lines up here with an RPR that is the highest of the 14-horse field but has an official ranking which is 4th bottom. This subsequently means Centaq goes out carrying comparatively less weight over this 2m 1f trip. The prior outing was 29 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Difficult to fancy on recent form, but the mare was in fine form this time last year. Raised seven pounds for winning at Punchestown on stable debut, she put in two very good efforts at Cork and Wexford. Two pounds lower mark today, and amateur Finn Buckley, who has had a couple of winners already in his short career, is able to reduce the mare's burden by a further seven pounds.

Became a bit frustrating really when with Sean Aherne but a surprise to see him chalked up as the rank outsider on debut for his new yard. This longer trip should suit, he goes well fresh and Danny Mullins is booked. He should outrun his odds at the very least.

Our Zebo won a point at the first attempt in April 2024 but did not jump well in his last race in a handicap chase at Cartmel off a mark of 96 in July 2024. He has since switched to hurdling, and after two wins, his hurdle mark is now 108 compared to his chase mark of only 87. He should find Downpatrick less daunting than Cartmel over fences and should win if ready for resuming his chasing career.

The model I run suggests Thehairyfella can win this one. Thehairyfella lines up here with the second highest RPR of this mid-size 9 runner field. He is the oldest runner of the bunch but is the only one to have really shown form coming into this. Form figures of P0-3P3, and if he can find a bit more, will go close today. The model has issued a low stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Our Zebo looks thrown in on his best chasing efforts but has had a busy season and looked a bit jaded over hurdles last month when beaten 33 lengths. So, a chance is taken on Mrs Biddle who has decent hurdles form and should make a staying chaser.
The trainer has got 2 entered in this race as they are stepping this one up in trip slightly with a good jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet.

This J P O'Brien trained 3-year-old colt will find this race a lot easier than when beaten three lengths behind the S bin Suroor trained Arabian Story in the 30-runner Britannia Stakes over one mile on good to firm ground at Ascot. So with D McMonagle back in the plate, it looks like a win today.
This 6-year-old exhibited some promise in a stronger race than this on her Listowel hurdle debut last month so must be a key player in this opening maiden.
Good run against 16 rivals last time out. Improving, went off 22/1. Much shorter price here but should take this hopefully. Should keep on well.

The model I run suggests Abel Mabel can win this one. Abel Mabel lines up here with a comparably high RPR but an official ranking leaving it well treated off this mark. Steps out carrying the joint lowest amount of initial weight to carry, and has Niall Moore on board relieving a further 5 lbs round this 2m 1f trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Two Become One has had a break but might be worth a small each way chance here since J Kennedy shows a 22% strike rate at Downpatrick and works well with G Elliot. Distance and ground should suit. Each way appeal.

Annarubyrose is a 4-year-old filly trained by Gavin Cromwell. She makes has shown some promise in two maiden hurdles, posting a RPR of 85. In each of those maiden hurdles, the race was won by the favorites, which strengthens the form. On her penultimate start, she finished 6th out of 12 behind Janes Harbour 8-11f. Of those who have since run, the 2nd out of 12, Radar Ahead, 10 lengths behind the winner, won a hurdle on the next start at Sligo. The 3rd out of 12, Bhean Saibhre, finished 2nd out of 18 in a maiden hurdle, then on the next start, unseated the rider two out when leading, so the form looks strong in the context of this race. She is out of an eight-race winning dam who proved to be a useful dual-purpose horse, winning four handicap hurdles (RPR of 137 for today's owner C B Poots of Annarubyrose) and won four times on the flat (Hughie Morrison). Sean Flanagan rides for Cromwell with 12 wins out of 238 wins and a 12% win strike rate, Annarubyrose has an outside chance of success, as rhis race won't take a lot of winning.

Placed on three of her last four starts in handicaps including a good effort when 2nd over todays C&D in May. Would be getting a bit of weight off some of these in a handicap but goes well fresh and none of her opponents are in any sort of form so looks decent value at 33's.

Betty Dutton has been progressively improving of late with finishes of 4th, 4th, and then 2nd last time out being the results of the last three outings. Last time out, that runner-up finish was as a 25/1 shot, and today is a big drop in terms of quality of opposition.

The model I run suggests Je Suis can win this one. Je Suis lines up here with the second highest RPR of this larger 11-horse race but has the joint lowest amount of initial weight to carry. Mr. Kennedy picks up the reins and relieves a further 7 lbs, which helps round this longer 2m 7f trip. Last out 13 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Stable mate Butchers Bill would have perhaps better credentials but Gina Moon made a decent debut over fences last time out ,looking booked for second spot before making a hash of the last. She should improve for that experience and if so might well be involved in the finish.

Despite blowing the start, this J P O'Brien-trained 3-year-old gelding did well to only be beaten 3/4 length in third of the eight runners behind the Donnacha O'Brien-trained Happy Pharoah over one mile four furlongs on good ground at Leopardstown 25 days ago. So, with D McMonagle in the saddle, he should prove hard to beat.

Defiantly made the frame despite falling out of the stalls on debut and has an obvious chance if getting away on terms but the selection should improve for this longer trip and can make her experience count.

Shakita was well beaten on sole racecourse run so far in October last year but has had time to come on since that run. Trainer Thomas Mullins had a recent winner with a 3yo filly. Significantly up in trip for this second start. Feasibly has place possibilities.

Chisum is a 5-year-old gelding owned and trained by Neil McKnight. Never counted on debut when a 200-1 shot in Navan maiden back in February. He is out of a pretty dire dam who is a sister to four individual winners who amassed a total of 19 wins, three of which were very smart: Firebird Flyer (RPR of 144), Premier Victory (RPR of 142), Spookydooky (RPR of 141). Neil McKnight is based in Loughbrickland, some 30.2 miles from Downpatrick, so local, and is 5/65 wins at the track showing a LSP of £2.50, last winning with Skinnhill at 7-2 on July 15th, 2024. Albeit a much shorter price, but at 50- 1 under Jordan Gainford, Chisum could potentially outrun current odds.

the model I run suggests an upset by Princess Georgie. This result has been driven by Princess Georgie having a comparably high RPR to the other runners here but goes out carrying at least 7 lbs less, and 1 stone less to the top weight and current market favourite. Tries cheek pieces for the first time to aid concentration and Conor Stone Walsh picks up the reins claiming a further 3 lbs off her back. This weight differential coupled with the new headgear, over this 2m 5f round trip might just be the answer to some recent struggles for form. Still a highly rated horse overall in regards to the wider field and maybe these changes can be the difference.
Has run better than bare result the last twice and nudges up a pound here after being unlucky in running last time. More than capable of winning one of these from around this mark.

Far From Dandy is an unexposed 3-year-old colt trained by Stephen Thorne. He makes his third start for the yard, having previously been trained by George Boughey. In his last two starts for Boughey, he finished 1-2, the latter in a novice stakes at Brighton where he was sent off 5-4f and was beaten 1/2l (RPR 77) by the James Tate-trained Gray David (received 6lb) RPR 78. That horse has since won at Nottingham and finished 3/7 in a Listed contest, then posted a career-high RPR of 105 in a Group 3 at Ascot. Far From Dandy has been highly tried in better races than today's fair, beaten 3l on stable debut, then got beat 7.25l in a rated race on last start posting RPR of 78-76 (both under an apprentice), so clearly retains ability. His trainer drops his charge down in grade and puts on first-time cheekpieces, and the booking of Colin Keane looks notable as replaces Kearney who's ridden more winner for trained 13 than any other jockey. Far From Dandy is likely to be a lot shorter price come post time, and on back form with Gray David, he could be a handicap blot in this company.

Dahlia Noir won a maiden at Gowan Park in April, then a respectable run back in handicaps at Navan followed by a fair run in a Leopardstown fillies handicap. Today at Killarney, she looks to have a very good chance of breaking her losing run in a lesser handicap. Each way advised as four places too at Bet365.
Naoi can get off the mark here, being upped in trip on handicap debut. Has been well backed each race. Looks to me like a plot job with a nice price.

Showed a little bit in a couple of runs as a two-year-old but showed a lot more on his return at the Curragh in mid-March. Finished in midfield but wasn’t given a hard ride and looked to have more to give at the line. Made handicap debut next time at Gowran over a mile and wasn’t disgraced, finishing 7th of 16. Has shown a bit of improvement in two subsequent handicap starts and was a close-up 3rd over a mile at Leopardstown last time. Kept to that trip here from a 2lb higher mark and chances have to be respected.

Faoladh looks a big price considering his overall profile and scope for improvement. He's shown glimpses of ability in stronger company and now drops into a winnable race where the setup could suit him well. The step back in trip combined with a more patient ride may unlock further progress. Connections have been quietly progressive with similar types, and at double-figure odds (at time of writing) he represents excellent value.

Henry De Bromhead has had 3 winners from his last 8 runners and I was admittedly surprised when I delved deeper to see that in the last year, his strike rate on the flat is virtually the same as his strike rate in NH. I think the horse is as big as it is due to the inexperienced jockey but the trainer has had a lot of Conditionals through his ranks over the years and can spot the good ones early. The jockey certainly looked capable enough last time out when 3rd of 16 on a 10/1 shot for the stable. The horse has a good draw and first time cheekpieces, looks worth an e/w bet at 14/1.

Edergoles Angel is a 3-year-old filly trained by W McCreery and ridden by N M Crosse, with no wins and a place rate of 33% in handicaps from six starts. She was fifth, beaten 6 lengths over 10 at Down Royal last time, but had been in better form previously and has already placed twice this season. So I'm giving her another each-way go today. She stays the trip well and has placed at the distance and on similar going, although she has yet to get her head in front. Her current mark of 64 looks very fair, and she runs from stall 5, which is neither a help nor a hindrance here at Killarney. The visor is retained, and she will probably be played late. If the pace is strong enough, she could be staying on into the frame again. Each-way possibilities in a very open-looking race today at 22/1.

Alpha Capture for Willie Mullins and top owners Munir and Souede has a great chance today. On his return after 10 months off, he should or could have won had the gaps opened for him at the right time. Didn't get a gap until it was too late. Should make amends here today under Colin Keane.

Just 3rd start for De Bromhead and won here last summer from 13 lbs lower. Shaped nicely LTO at Leopardstown over 7f and with the jockey claim here 4 lbs below last winning AW mark. Surely primed for this with good draw.

Last year Evening Blossom won back-to-back races on good ground at the one-mile distance. This season she has raced three times. Her second race saw her enter the winner's enclosure at Limerick, having secured a half-length victory. She was then pitched into a higher class race and finished nearer last than first. Today she is back in calmer waters, so I'm taking her to bounce back and run well against today's rivals.

A David Marnane trained 5-year-old who has had 18 races on the flat, winning 3 times and has finished in the frame 3 times. This mare has won her last 5 races on the bounce, winning last time out on a 6k fillies handicap over 1 mile at Limerick on good going, ridden by today's jockey Darragh O'Sullivan claiming 7 lbs when leading inside the final furlong to win by 3/4 of a length. She is in a 10k handicap over 1 mile on good going and the jockey is claiming 7 lbs again. She is in decent form at present and has won 6 times on the a/w. She won on good ground last time out over this distance, has a good e/w shout in this race today.

Twice a winner over 1 mile including an impressive win last time out at Limerick last month. Carries an 8lbs penalty in a better race but still gets in with bottom weight and a big chance if building on that last performance.

Grey Leader is a 5yo mare trained by Joseph G Murphy. She finished 5/8 in this race last year and was sent off 11-10f. The 1/8 Independent Expert has since won off a 6lb higher mark; the 2/8 Physique won two starts later (2lb higher mark); the 3/8 Shigar won two starts later. Our selection, who didn't get the clearest of runs that day, won on the next start at Gowran in a big field handicap (5lb higher) on 85. The 6/8 Sea Chariot won three runs later. So why is Grey Leader 40-1 today as she runs off the same mark as her Galway win on 85 and was unlucky in running? The reasons for the huge 40-1 may be the Racing Post's suggestion that he may need rain, but hhe did win at Listowel on good ground and has won on yielding and heavy ground. His chances of winning will certainly increase if there is a downpour. Willie Mullins has a hot market leader in the shape of Alpha Capture at 13-8. She is definitely of significant interest at 40- 1. Just hope all is well after two substandard runs in May (Ben Coen rides).

His mark is only two pounds above that of his last win, and Gavin Ryan who has twice been successful on the gelding is back on board. It's best part of ten months since Imposing Supreme was last seen on a racecourse, but he was only narrowly denied when returning from a similar break twelve months ago. Odds look too big for a horse with his form figures.
Fairly well-bred filly. Should have a bit of stamina and will have every chance of staying this far to win for the Harrington team.
MATRICE has been placed in two races from four starts. Sixth over 1m 2f at Fairyhouse on her latest outing last month. Upped in trip to 1m 3f should suit and could well be able to win this race.

Thilos is better than his bare form suggests and could be primed to strike now stepping into handicap company for the first time. He shaped well in maidens behind solid opposition and has hinted at ability without being fully asked for it. The switch to handicap looks significant, and connections have placed him in a winnable race. With natural progression expected and the blinkers retained, there's a chance he can make a step forward today.

On the face of it 10th of 12 on her racecourse debut doesn’t sound good but she was beaten a little over 6 lengths and looked in need of the experience. Matched that form last time when 4th at Down Royal stepping up in trip and over a slightly longer trip here can reward each way support.
Magnolia Drive is fitted with first-time cheekpieces here and can gain a first success now upped in trip, which is likely to bring about significant improvement.

The market is made up of a couple of horses at 2/1 or shorter, but neither looks the type to be worth siding with at short prices. This unexposed outsider could get amongst the places in this 9-runner field. The horse is pro-ridden for only the second time, and the jockey booked has a very good record at the course. The trainer's last runner won, and this horse looks to have been given mainly quiet runs to date. Racing comments such as 'slowly away' and followed up by 'made late ground' are just the types that pop up at big prices (usually backed) when they race off potentially lenient marks. Hopefully, that will be the case again here. Jockey bookings suggest it could be.

This maiden, with limited racing experience, is donning a tongue strap for the first time. She recently finished 12th in a handicap race at Tipperary 12 days ago. Now, with a significant increase in trip, this 3-year-old could very well surprise us, especially with the jockey's claim aiding her performance. Each-way odds at 40/1 look like a solid bet.

The model I run suggests Gorthill can win this one. Gorthill lines up here with the second highest RPR of this 8 runner field and has the highest official ranking. Doesn't look overly penalized for it in the weights and is the only horse to have shown signs of some decent form. Figures of P134-2 and needs to build on that to get over the line first again. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
